description: Advanced C++ Practice: Exception Handling, File Handling, Pointers, Dynamic Memory, Copy Constructor and Friend Functions

questions.questionText: Which keywords are commonly used for exception handling in C++?
questions.explanation: C++ exception handling primarily uses try, catch and throw.

questions.questionText: Which keyword is used to generate an exception explicitly?
questions.explanation: The throw keyword is used to explicitly raise an exception.

questions.questionText: Which block contains code that may generate an exception?
questions.explanation: Code that may throw an exception is placed inside a try block.

questions.questionText: Which block handles an exception thrown from a try block?
questions.explanation: A catch block handles an exception thrown from the associated try block.

questions.questionText: What does catch(...) represent in C++?
questions.optionD: It can catch an exception of any type
questions.explanation: The ellipsis catch handler can catch exceptions of any type.

questions.questionText: Which header is commonly used for standard exception classes such as std::exception?
questions.explanation: The <exception> header provides the standard exception base class and related facilities.

questions.questionText: Which class is commonly used as a base class for standard C++ exceptions?
questions.explanation: std::exception is the standard base class for many standard library exceptions.

questions.questionText: Which mode opens a file for reading?
questions.explanation: ios::in opens a file for input or reading.

questions.questionText: Which mode opens a file for writing?
questions.explanation: ios::out opens a file for output or writing.

questions.questionText: Which mode opens a file and writes new data at the end of the existing content?
questions.explanation: ios::app opens the file in append mode, so new output is added at the end.

questions.questionText: Which C++ class is commonly used to read data from a file?
questions.explanation: std::ifstream is used for file input or reading.

questions.questionText: Which C++ class is commonly used to write data to a file?
questions.explanation: std::ofstream is used for file output or writing.

questions.questionText: Which class can be used for both reading from and writing to files?
questions.explanation: std::fstream supports both input and output file operations.

questions.questionText: Which operator is used to obtain the address of a variable?
questions.explanation: The address-of operator & returns the memory address of an object.

questions.questionText: Which operator is used to dereference a pointer?
questions.explanation: The unary * operator dereferences a pointer and accesses the object it points to.

questions.questionText: Which operator is commonly used to access a member through a pointer to an object?
questions.explanation: The -> operator accesses a member through a pointer to an object.

questions.questionText: Which operator is used to dynamically allocate memory in C++?
questions.explanation: The new operator dynamically allocates memory and can initialize the allocated object.

questions.questionText: Which operator is used to release memory allocated using new?
questions.explanation: Memory allocated for a single object using new should normally be released using delete.

questions.questionText: Which operator is used to release dynamically allocated arrays created using new[]?
questions.explanation: Memory allocated using new[] should be released using delete[].

questions.questionText: What is a memory leak?
questions.optionA: Memory that is accessed through a valid pointer
questions.optionB: Dynamically allocated memory that is no longer accessible but has not been released
questions.explanation: A memory leak occurs when dynamically allocated memory is not properly released and can no longer be accessed.

questions.questionText: What is a copy constructor?
questions.optionA: A constructor used to initialize an object from another object of the same or compatible type
questions.optionB: A constructor that accepts only integers
questions.optionC: A constructor that deletes an object
questions.optionD: A constructor used only for inheritance
questions.explanation: A copy constructor initializes a new object using an existing object.

questions.questionText: Which is a typical declaration of a copy constructor for class Test?
questions.explanation: A common copy constructor declaration is Test(const Test& other).

questions.questionText: What is the purpose of a friend function?
questions.optionB: It can access private and protected members of a class
questions.optionC: It can only access public members
questions.optionD: It automatically becomes a member function
questions.explanation: A friend function is not a member of the class but can access its private and protected members.

questions.questionText: Which keyword is used to declare a friend function inside a class?
questions.explanation: The friend keyword declares a function or class as a friend.

questions.questionText: What is the output? int x = 10; int* p = &x; cout << *p;
questions.explanation: p stores the address of x, and *p dereferences the pointer to access the value 10.
